title: Locally Solvable Radicals via Wilson Radical Sets and Subgroup Lattices
summary: For a group $G$, let $S(G)$ be the set of elements $g \in G$ such that $\langle g,x\rangle$ is solvable for all $x \in G$. We study when $S(G)$ coincides with the locally solvable radical $R_{\mathrm{L}\mathfrak{S}}(G)$. Using Wilson's profinitely convergent word sequences, we show that, for every locally (solvable-by-finite) group $G$ and every Wilson sequence $ω$, $$ R_{\mathrm{L}\mathfrak{S}}(G) = R_{\mathrm{L}\mathfrak{R}}(G) = S(G) = W_ω(G).$$ We also obtain four-conjugate and seven-commutator descriptions of radical membership, together with a two-conjugate result for torsion elements…
